title.narrative: 15th replenishment of the African Development Fund

description.narrative:
The African Development Fund is the Bank Group’s provider of concessional lending and grant financing. The ADF contributes to poverty reduction and economic and social sustainable development by financing projects and reforms and providing technical assistance and capacity building in low-income African countries that are not eligible to borrow from the AfDB.
The 15th replenishment of the ADF (2020-2022) will focus on two strategic pillars: the first is to develop quality and sustainable infrastructure that provides impetus for job-creating private sector investments, and which promotes sustainable development. The second is on human, governance and institutional capacity development to enable people to participate in, and benefit from, job creation opportunities for inclusive growth. The two pillars will be anchored around the crosscutting themes of gender, climate change, governance and private sector development to foster inclusive growth and strengthen resilience.

Updated results on the ADF is found in the 2024 Annual report (27.05.2025): https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/annual-report-2024
Based on the AfDB’s Annual Development Effectiveness Review, the following results can be reported in relation to select Danish priorities as set out in the Organisation Strategy – for all African countries and for ADF countries, respectively.
Climate change and green growth: Improved ‘installed renewable capacity’, ‘new renewable power capacity installed’, ‘emission reductions in energy’, ‘people with new or improved access to water and sanitation’ as well as ‘new operations with climate informed design’. Deteriorated ‘people with new electricity connections’ whereas ‘access to electricity’ and ‘access to at least basic drinking water services’ remains the same, while the latter is still below the 2015 baseline.
Level 1: ‘Access to electricity’: all African Countries: remained at 56 %. ADF: up from 41 to 44 %.
‘Installed renewable capacity’: all African countries: up from 54 to 56 GW. ADF: up from 26 to 27 GW.
‘Access to at least basic drinking water services’: all African countries: remained at 69 %. ADF: remained at 59 %.
Level 2: ‘New renewable power capacity installed’: all African countries: up from 72 to 113 MW. ADF: up from 56 to 78 MW.
‘People with new electricity connections’: all African countries: down from 1306 to 1300 thousands. ADF: down from 1306 to 1098 thousands. ‘Of whom women’: all African countries: down from 616 to 613 thousands. ADF: down from 616 to 518 thousands.
‘Emission reductions in energy’: all African countries: up from 1066 to 2626 thousand tons CO2. ADF: up from 1030 to 2572 thousand tons CO2.
‘People with new or improved access to water and sanitation’: all African countries: up from 12,2 to 12,3 million. ADF: down from 9,2 to 8,5 million.
Level 3: ‘New operations with climate informed design’: all African countries: up from 92 to 94 %. ADF: up from 97 to 98 %.
